editorial:
Imagine having a job that lets you travel the whole world and meet beautiful people every single week. That is exactly the life of the main character in this breezy old-school rom-com. He is a reporter who uses his work trips as an excuse to flirt and chase women in every city he visits. While he is happily married, he just cannot seem to stop his wandering eye. The whole movie feels like a lighthearted game of cat and mouse, blending funny misunderstandings with the kind of charm you only find in movies from the early forties. It is basically a story about a man who thinks he is smoother than he actually is, and it keeps you smiling throughout.

You will love how the fast talking and quick jokes keep the energy high. The acting is snappy, and the pacing never feels slow, though some of the humor is definitely a product of its time. If you enjoy classic stories about cheating spouses getting their comeuppance, you will have a blast. It is a great pick for a lazy Sunday afternoon. You can easily find this one to rent on Apple TV or search for a remastered version to add to your physical Blu-ray collection if you love owning movie history. It looks great on any screen!
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the husband's secrets finally catch up with him. His wife finds out about his constant flirting and the games he has been playing across the globe. After a series of funny and tense confrontations, he realizes that no amount of international travel is better than his marriage. He finally stops his cheating ways, asks for forgiveness, and the couple reconciles. It ends on a happy note with the husband choosing loyalty over his ego.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic Hollywood comedies and stories about marriage mishaps.
